name: price_impact_reversion_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Large trades (>5x median trade size) cause temporary price impact that partially reverts within 2-5 minutes. In Indian mid-cap equities where liquidity is thinner, a single large market order can push the price 10-30 bps beyond fair value. Market makers and informed traders step in to capture the reversion, but retail traders who observe the move interpret it as momentum and pile in, slowing the reversion. The inefficiency persists because: (1) detecting large trades requires tick-level monitoring, (2) the reversion window is narrow (2-5 min), and (3) distinguishing informed large trades (no reversion) from uninformed ones (reversion) requires context. We use VWAP deviation as a filter: large trades that push price far from VWAP are more likely uninformed liquidity-seeking orders.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.

indicators.name: impact_bps
indicators.formula: (close - close[1]) / close[1] * 10000 on bars where large_trade_flag == 1

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; impacts in high-VIX tend to be informed (no reversion)
filters.volume_filter: bar volume > 2x SMA(volume, 20) (confirm the large trade bar)

weaknesses: Cannot distinguish informed vs uninformed large trades with certainty. Trading against an informed institutional buyer means catching a falling knife / fighting momentum.
In NIFTY 100 stocks ranked 51-100, liquidity can dry up suddenly, making exit at target price difficult and widening actual slippage beyond the 3 bps assumption.
Result season (Jan-Feb, Apr-May, Jul-Aug, Oct-Nov) increases false signals as earnings-driven large trades are informed and don't revert.
prior_art: Bouchaud, Farmer & Lillo (2009) 'How Markets Slowly Digest Changes in Supply and Demand' — foundational work on price impact and reversion. Almgren & Chriss (2000) 'Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions'. In India, SEBI's impact cost reports for index constituents provide empirical basis.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe; order book data integration. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
